column2: Schneider Electric LP1K TeSys K Miniature Contactor

Schneider Electric's TeSys K silent miniature contactors are reliable contactors with long mechanical and electrical life. The LP1K series is a DC powered contactor and is a silent contactor ideal for use in areas sensitive to noise and high interference mains power. TeSys K contactors are quick and easy to set up while maintaining compliance with international standards. Due to the special armature structure design, all devices in the series conveniently have a common physical size and panel footprint.

Features and Benefits: Built-in auxiliary contacts add switching functionality Screw connection: IP20 finger-protected terminals compliant with both North American and international terminal markings Compatible with panel mounting with screws or DIN rail mounting Built-in coil with rectifier Easy-to-install accessories Instant auxiliary Contacts Flexible control circuitry for a wide range of applications High fault short circuit current rating for increased flexibility in component selection
What do the usage categories AC1 and AC3 mean for TeSys contactors?
Contactor usage categories define make/break current values ​​based on the type of load being controlled and operating cycle conditions.
AC-1: Applies to all AC equipment with a power factor of 0.95 or higher. Usage examples: resistive loads, heaters, power distribution, etc.
AC-3: Applies to three-phase squirrel cage motors where a break occurs during motor operation.
Usage examples: All three-phase squirrel cage motors, elevators, escalators, conveyors, bucket elevators, compressors, pumps, mixers, air conditioning units, etc.
Are TeSys K contactors suitable for use category AC4 applications?
The LP1K series supports a maximum voltage of 440 V ac in category AC4.
Is the TeSys K series a double break pole type contactor?
Yes, TeSys K series realizes double breaking of poles by parallel movement.

AC-3: Applies to three-phase squirrel cage motors where a break occurs during motor operation. Usage examples: All three-phase squirrel cage motors, elevators, escalators, conveyors, bucket elevators, compressors, pumps, mixers, air conditioning units, etc.

Drill　bits　are　attachments　for　power　tools,　like　handheld　or　industrial　size　drills
They　generally　come　in　different　shapes　or　sizes　and　drastically　reduce　themAnual　work　needed　for　construction,　electrical　ormAsonry　applications

This　generally　means　the　length　of　the　entire　drill　bit　itself　is　significantly　longer　for　diameter　it　has
As　an　example,　a　mechanic　drill　bit　will　have　a　much　shorter　flute　and　therefore　have　a　much　smaller　overall　length
An　acronym　for　High-speed　steel,　HSS　is　generally　the　go-to　type　of　steel　needed　for　drill　bits　due　to　their　excellent　heat　resistance　at　high　speeds
As　a　standard　drill　can　spin　upwards　of　around　500　-　700rpm,　the　friction　can　cause　a　substantial　build-up　of　heat
Something　which　would　not　be　wanted　when　working　with　wood　and　plastic.

When the magnetic flux interlinks with the loop, a current flows in the GND wire, which creates a voltage that becomes noise. In such cases, cutting the loop can prevent noise due to magnetic flux linkage.

This axial fan does not use either. Ceramic bearings have been tested to be more cost-effective to manufacture and have a longer service life than standard ball/sleeve bearing fans. Its features include extremely low friction, quiet and smooth operation, and virtually no static electricity.

What can I use an axial fan with?

Axial fans are used in all industries where cooling of components and equipment is essential. Fans cool surfaces by drawing air or pushing hot air out. Here are some of the most common applications for DC axial fans.
Server Racks - Axial fans are used to cool hubs, routers, and patch panels.
Electrical Cabinets and Enclosures - Installed in cabinets and enclosures to cool and protect components and prevent premature failure.
Laptops and Tower Computers - Compact DC fans are ideal for integration into computers and equipment. The frame size is small and thin.

Axial fans are a type of fan commonly used in everyday applications such as air conditioners and computers. This allows air and gas (depending on the application) to flow straight along the fan's axis at varying speeds. Both the inlet and outlet can have axial airflow. The most common types tend to have fewer blades than traditional ducted and centrifugal fans, which operate similarly.

column2: Frequently Asked Questions – LP-50F 1KΩ Linear Displacement Sensor (MIDORI PRECISIONS):
1/ What is the LP-50F 1KΩ linear displacement sensor?
The LP-50F is a conductive-plastic potentiometer that converts linear motion into a proportional change in electrical resistance. It delivers reliable position feedback in a compact form factor.
2/ What industries and applications commonly use this sensor?

Typical applications include automotive testing (ejector strokes, wheel alignment), injection molding machines, vending machines, driving simulators, material position control, and general motion measurement.

The LP-50F uses a sliding wiper over a resistive track. As the shaft moves along its travel, the wiper position changes the resistance between its two end terminals and the wiper terminal. This variable resistance can be measured directly or converted into a voltage/current signal for position feedback.
5/ How many wires does it have? Three wires: two ends of the resistive element and one wiper (output).

6/ How do I get a usable voltage or current signal? Use the sensor in a voltage divider configuration. Excite the two end terminals with a known DC voltage, then measure the wiper voltage. For current loops (4 - 20 mA), feed the wiper voltage into a signal conditioner or dedicated transmitter.

7/ Can I interface it directly with a PLC or data acquisition system? Yes, by pairing with a signal conditioner that outputs 0 - 5 V, 0 - 10 V, or 4 - 20 mA you can feed the position data directly into most PLC analog inputs or DAQ modules.
8/ What is the recommended mounting procedure?
- Secure the sensor body with two M3 or M4 screws, avoiding over-torque.
- Align the shaft axis precisely with the moving part’s travel path to prevent side loads and binding.
- Use flexible couplings or anti-rotation brackets if necessary to isolate mounting forces.
9/ How do I protect it from dust and moisture? Fit appropriate seals or boots around the shaft interface. Keep mounting surfaces clean and consider IP-rated enclosures for harsh environments.
10/ How do I calibrate the sensor?
- Move the shaft to the mechanical zero position and record the corresponding resistance or voltage.
- Move it to full travel (50 mm) and record the second reading.
- Use these two data points to scale the output in your control system.
11/ What maintenance is required? Periodic inspection every 6 - 12 months or after 1000 hours of operation:
- Clean the shaft and housing of debris.
- Apply light machine oil to the sliding surfaces.
- Check wiring integrity and mounting bolts.
12/ Is there a version with a return spring? Yes, the LP-50FB adds a spring-return mechanism and can achieve ± 0.2% FS linearity.

Polyurethane offers superior elasticity and abrasion resistance, whereas nylon provides higher burst pressure but is more rigid and prone to scuffing.

The Importance of a Quality Crimp When using a crimping tool on a terminal, two crimps are made at the same time: one is the electrical connection between the conductor and the terminal; the other is the insulation crimp, which provides strain relief against vibration and tension. It is important that the electrical connection is airtight, with no air gaps between the strands and the terminal. FAQ: 40W ISHIZAKI ELECTRIC SURE SG-31 Handheld Heat Cutter:
1. What is the SURE SG-31 and what is it used for?

The SURE SG-31 is a 40 W handheld thermal cutter whose blade generates its own heat, allowing precise, dust-free cutting of materials like polystyrene foam, urethane sponge, nets, loops, PP tape and thin plastics without producing waste chips or fraying.
2. What are the main technical specifications?

column3: A-type: approx. 400 °C
I-type: approx. 500 °C

column2: 3. Which blades and attachments are available?
A-type blade (400 °C): standard for foam cutting
I-type blade (500 °C): ideal for nets, loops and tougher plastics
G-type and H-type blades: specialized shapes for net-only or loop-only cutting
C, D, F types and others: for cutting textile, acrylic threads, resin sheets, etc.
Quick-release driver bar design makes blade swaps tool-free
4. How do I set up and operate the SG-31?
Securely fasten the chosen blade into the driver slot.
Plug into a properly grounded AC 100 V outlet.
Turn on the power switch and wait 30–60 seconds for the blade to reach operating temperature.
Feed the hot blade gently through the material at a consistent speed to achieve smooth, precise cuts.
After use, switch off, unplug and allow the blade to cool fully before storage.
5. What materials can the SG-31 cut smoothly?
Nets, ropes and thin plastic tubing
These materials slice cleanly without fraying or dust generation.
6. What safety precautions should I follow?
Wear heat-resistant gloves, safety glasses and a dust-mask or respirator.
Never touch the blade during or immediately after operation.
Keep flammable materials and vapors away from the heat source.
Avoid kinking or stretching the power cord near the hot blade.
Operate in a well-ventilated area or under fume extraction to avoid inhaling off-gassing.
7. How should I maintain and clean the SG-31?
After each session, let the blade cool then brush or wipe off residue with a dry cloth.
Do not immerse the unit or use corrosive solvents.
Inspect the power cord, switch and connections monthly; replace immediately if insulation is damaged.
Store in a dry place away from direct sunlight or high humidity.
8. What common issues might occur and how do I troubleshoot them?
Blade won’t heat: verify outlet voltage, switch position and cord integrity.
Insufficient temperature: blade may be worn—replace or switch to a higher-temperature type.
Burning smell or smoke: stop immediately, let the blade cool, then clear built-up residue.
Unit shuts off unexpectedly: the heating element or switch may be faulty—seek authorized service.
9. Where can I get replacement blades and accessories?

Genuine spare blades and attachments (A, I, G, H and others) are available through ISHIZAKI ELECTRIC’s distributors as QTE Technologies (qtetech.com/en). You can also purchase replacement power cords, mounting hooks and specialized cutting tables.
10. What warranty and technical support are offered?

The SG-31 comes with a 12-month warranty covering manufacturing defects (wear parts such as blades excluded). Contact your local ISHIZAKI ELECTRIC dealer (QTE Technologies - qtetech.com/en) or the official support hotline for spare parts, technical manuals and troubleshooting guidance.

Daikin Industries LT3030A-10 Oil Cooler (300 L/min, 829 × 205mm) - In-Depth Technical Guide and FAQ:

The LT3030A-10 is a water‐cooled oil cooler designed by Daikin Industries for lubrication, hydraulic drive, and compressor cooling systems. It delivers a maximum oil flow of 300 L/min while requiring only a modest cooling water flow. Freedoms in installation and robust construction make it suitable for diverse industrial environments.

This oil cooler features copper heat exchanger tubes brazed to spiral fins, providing excellent thermal conductivity and corrosion resistance. The spiral‐fin design agitates the oil to enhance turbulent mixing and heat transfer efficiency. Legs welded directly to the frame allow secure mounting and vibration resistance.

Oil flows through internal copper tubes while cooling water passes around the brazed spiral fins. Heat from the oil conducts through the tube walls into the fins, where the water absorbs it. The spiral fins induce a swirling motion that maintains high turbulence, maximizing the thermal exchange between oil and water without manual adjustment of flow paths.
- Ensure clearances around the cooler for airflow and maintenance access.
- Position the cooler so that the water inlet sits below the outlet to facilitate automatic air release.
- Weld the integrated legs securely to the machine frame or base to withstand operational vibrations.
- Connect oil and water lines using pressure‐rated fittings compatible with 300 L/min oil flow.
-Install an air‐bleed valve at the highest fin channel point to purge trapped air.
- Pre‐fill the fin channels with cooling water via the bleed valve before starting the system.
- Simultaneously start the oil pump and cooling‐water supply, monitoring pressure and flow rates.
- Measure inlet and outlet oil temperatures to verify cooling performance; adjust water flow as needed.
- Avoid dry operation of either circuit; ensure continuous oil and water circulation.
- After shutdown, run the water pump briefly to dissipate residual heat from the fins.

To prolong cooler life and maintain performance, cooling water quality must meet industrial standards for hardness, pH, and suspended solids. Poor water quality accelerates fin fouling and corrosion. Regular monitoring of flow rate, temperature, and water chemistry is recommended to ensure consistent heat exchange efficiency.
- Daily or per‐shift: rinse fins with clean water to remove oil deposits and debris.
- Every 3 - 6 months: inspect brazed joints and piping for leaks; replace degraded seals.
- Replace cooling water periodically and add corrosion inhibitors if using reclaimed or construction water.
- Tighten weld‐mounted legs and pressure fittings to prevent vibration-induced loosening.
- Immediately repair or re‐brazing any leaks in tube‐to‐fin joints to avoid cross-contamination.
8.1/ Can I use seawater as the cooling medium?
No. The cooler is rated only for fresh water or construction water to prevent salt‐induced corrosion.
8.2/ What is the optimal water flow relative to oil flow?
Aim for a water flow of 1.2 - 1.5 times the oil flow (360 - 450 L/min) for maximum thermal performance.
8.3/ How do I purge air from the fin channels?
Open the bleed valve at the fin’s highest point until water flows steadily without air bubbles.
No. Thanks to 360° mounting flexibility, the cooler can be oriented to suit space constraints.
8.5/ How often should I replace the cooling water?
Replace every 3 - 6 months or sooner if water quality tests indicate elevated hardness, pH drift, or high particulates.
Common causes include fin fouling, low water flow, corrosion, or air trapped in the channels.
8.7/ How do I inspect for internal leaks?
Perform a pressure test on the oil and water circuits separately, monitoring for pressure drop over time.
8.8/ Can the cooler handle variable flow rates?
Yes, but maintain minimum flows to avoid dry‐out of tubes or fins, which can lead to overheating and damage.

111-64870,TOHNICHI QSP3N4 Torque wrench (0.6 - 3Nm),

column2: 1/ How do I change the torque setting?
Remove the lock pin, use the #931 adjustment key to rotate the end cap to the target Nm, then reinsert the lock pin.
The output torque will be within +/-3% of the set value. For a 3 Nm setting, actual torque will be 2.91 - 3.09 Nm.
After 1000 tightening cycles or every six months, whichever comes first. High-frequency use or harsh environments may require more frequent checks.
4/ Can I use it to loosen fasteners?
No. QSP3N4’s click mechanism is unidirectional. Using it in reverse may damage the internal clutch.
Ideal for M1.6 - M4 screws and small bolts in electronics, instrumentation, and precision assemblies.
6/ Why isn’t it clicking at the set torque?

Possible causes: degraded spring tension, dirt in the mechanism, or incorrect adjustment. Send for service if cleaning and re-setting do not restore click. Please contact QTE Technologies (qtetech.com/en).
7/ Can I swap heads or use extensions?
Only use 1/4″ sq. drive extensions rated for torque-wrench use. Avoid impact-rated extensions - they can alter delivered torque.
Wipe with a dry cloth after each use. Do not immerse in solvent. Lightly oil external surfaces, avoiding the click mechanism.
9/ What if it feels stiff or sticks?
Dirt or grit may have entered the clutch. Remove adjustment key, cycle through full range, then gently tap the handle to dislodge debris. If problem persists, return for repair.
QSP3N4 is right-hand only. For left-hand or reversible click-type needs, consult the QL or QSP-MH series.
11/ How do I verify its performance?
Use a calibrated torque tester or gauge. Test at 20%, 60%, and 100% of full scale to confirm accuracy.

FAQ for ENDO KOGYO EHW-120R Air Balancer (120kg, 1.9m, 0.6MPa):

The EHW-120R is an air-powered wire hoist designed to lift, lower, and hold loads up to 120kg with a 1.9m stroke.
It’s widely used in automotive assembly, machinery maintenance, chemical plants, clean rooms, and any production line requiring ergonomic lifting and precise positioning.
2/ What are the air supply requirements?
Maintain a clean, dry, oil-free compressed air supply at 0.5 - 0.6MPa to ensure smooth operation and cylinder longevity.
Recommended minimum airflow is 50 L/min, with piping of at least φ10mm (φ12mm preferred) to minimize pressure drop.
3/ How do I install the EHW-120R?
- Securely hang the balancer from a structural beam or trolley rated at least four times the maximum load.
- Install an air shut-off valve within 1m of the balancer for emergency isolation.
- Route the air supply tubing straight to the inlet, avoiding sharp bends or kinks.
- Tighten all fittings and check gaskets before pressurizing.
4/ What is the basic operating procedure?
- Open the air shut-off valve and confirm system pressure at 0.6MPa.
- Use the pendant pushbutton to raise or lower the load; higher buttons increase speed, lower buttons decrease speed.
- Release all buttons to lock the load in position automatically via the internal locking valve.
- Adjust fine-tuning speed control knob on the pendant for precise positioning.
- Daily: Inspect for air leaks at fittings and clean dust off the hoist body.
- Weekly: Lubricate guide rollers and seals with silicone oil.
- Monthly: Disassemble and inspect one-way valve and replace O-rings if showing wear.

Frequently Asked Questions about HAKKO FG100B-83 Soldering Iron Tip Thermometer:
The FG100B-83 is an electronic soldering iron tip thermometer designed to measure tip temperature from 0 to 700°C with 1°C resolution.
2/ What type of thermocouple sensor does it use?
It uses a slim K-type thermocouple sensor (AS5000), optimized for fast and accurate readings.
3/ How long does the sensor last?
The AS5000 sensor maintains measurement accuracy for up to 1,500 readings - around 30 times longer than the conventional sensor.
4/ Can I replace the sensor? What are the replacement parts?
Yes. The AS5000 sensor (P/N 191-212) is replaceable. For measurements above 500°C, a specialized probe such as P/N: A1310 is recommended.
5/ How do I turn the unit on and off, and change the battery?
Press and hold the power button for about 2 seconds to turn on or off. It uses a 9V alkaline battery, and automatically shuts off after 3 minutes of inactivity below 100°C.
6/ What are the AUTO HOLD and MAX HOLD functions?
AUTO HOLD ends the measurement when the tip reaches a stable temperature. MAX HOLD displays the highest temperature recorded during the measurement cycle.
7/ How can I record or export measurement data?
By using an connection to compatible HAKKO soldering stations (e.g., FN-1010, FX-805), you can transfer AUTO HOLD or MAX HOLD readings directly into your station’s log.
8/ How often should I calibrate the FG100B-83?
Calibration is recommended every 6 to 12 months or after approximately 200 to 300 measurements to ensure ongoing accuracy.
9/ How do I clean and store the thermometer?
Wipe the housing with a soft, dry cloth. Store the unit in its protective case away from humidity and extreme temperatures.
10/ Any tips to prolong its lifespan?
Avoid excessive force on the sensor tip, use high quality solder and flux to reduce corrosion, and replace the sensor at the first sign of measurement drift.
11/ What does the “burnt out” error mean?
It indicates a damaged or disconnected sensor, requiring immediate replacement of the AS5000 sensor.
12/ Why is the measured temperature lower than expected?
Possible causes include a worn sensor, poor tip-to-sensor contact, or low battery voltage.
13/ The unit won’t power on - what should I check?
Verify the battery is installed correctly and charged, ensure the sensor connector is fully seated, and contact service - QTE Technologies (qtetech.com/en) if the mainboard is suspected faulty.
14/ How does FG100B-83 differ from FG100B-84?
The FG100B-84 offers a longer, flexible sensor lead for hard-to-reach tips, while the FG100B-83 has a compact integrated sensor for quick measurements.
15/ What are typical applications for this thermometer?
It’s used to standardize soldering tip temperature in electronic component manufacturing, PCB quality control, and training of soldering technicians.

Frequently Asked Questions about the HAKKO 393-1 Vacuum Pick-Up Tool:
1/ What is the HAKKO 393-1 Vacuum Pick-Up Tool?

The 393-1 is a portable, manual dropper-type vacuum pick-up pen designed for handling micro and surface-mounted components without the need for any power source or external pump. It’s made from anti-static materials and fits easily in your pocket for precision electronic assembly work.
2/ What is its maximum pick-up capacity?

The tool can generate up to 40 gf of suction force, which is achieved when using the largest nozzle/pad combination (A1165 or A1486 nozzle with a φ10 mm pad) and depends on the component’s surface finish.
3/ What are its dimensions and weight?
The 393-1 has a slim, pen-type body measuring 13 mm in diameter and 132 mm in length. Its weight is approximately 19 g, excluding any attached nozzle or pad.
4/ Which nozzles and pads are compatible with the 393-1?

column3: Nozzles (only A1165 or A1486 fit the tool):

A1486 – straight 1.1 mm nozzle with stopper

column3: Pads (conductive silicone rubber):

column4: A1311 – φ10 mm, ~40 gf suction Nozzles must be used in combination with pads to create effective suction.

column2: 5/ How do I operate the vacuum pick-up tool?

column3: Select and attach the appropriate nozzle and pad.
Press the button on the pen body to expel air and create vacuum.
Place the pad gently onto the component surface to pick it up.
Release the button to secure the component.
Press again to release the component or to swap pads/nozzles as needed.

column2: 6/ Is it safe for handling ESD-sensitive components?
Yes. The body, nozzle, and pads are made of anti-static (ESD-safe) materials to prevent electrostatic discharge during handling of delicate electronic parts.
7/ Can I store spare nozzles and pads on the tool?
Spare nozzle and pad combinations can be conveniently stored in the rear end of the pen for quick access during work sessions.
8/ Can I use the 393-1 to vacuum dust or debris?
No. The tool is specifically designed for picking up micro-components. Vacuuming dust or other particulate matter can clog the internal filter and render the tool inoperable.

Frequently Asked Questions for TRUSCO NAKAYAMA TDP-15 (#1200, 15 μm):
TRUSCO NAKAYAMA TDP-15 is an oil-based diamond paste formulated for final polishing, featuring uniformly dispersed 15 μm diamond abrasives in a 5 g tube.
Grit #1200 denotes the average particle size of the abrasive grains—approximately 15 μm—which is ideal for ultra‐fine polishing and producing mirror-like surface finishes.
3. Which materials are compatible with this diamond paste?
Precision mechanical components requiring high gloss
Mirror surfaces before plating or coating
4. How should I apply the diamond paste correctly?
Choose an appropriate polishing medium (lapping plate, felt pad, or polishing cloth).
Dispense a small “pea-sized” amount of paste onto the medium.
Polish the workpiece with light, uniform pressure until the desired sheen is reached.
Inspect under bright light to identify areas needing additional paste.
Clean off residual paste with a suitable solvent (e.g., petroleum ether or isopropyl alcohol).
5. How do I clean tools and parts after polishing?
Wipe excess paste off with a clean, lint-free cloth.
Use a mild solvent (petroleum ether, acetone, or isopropyl alcohol) to remove any remaining residue.
Rinse with water or a neutral detergent solution if compatible.
Dry thoroughly before further processing or storage.
6. What are the packaging details and product code?
Package: Small plastic tube with a screw-cap
Keep the cap tightly closed to prevent contamination and solvent evaporation.
Store in a dry location at 0–40 °C, away from direct sunlight and heat sources.
Avoid storing near corrosive chemicals or open flames.
8. What is the typical shelf life of this diamond paste?
When stored correctly, the diamond paste maintains optimal performance for 1–2 years. Refer to the datasheet or tube label for the exact expiration date.

1. What is the AS ONE SAS-3000 flared sterilizer used for?

The SAS-3000 is a compact benchtop dry-heat sterilizer designed to raise sample temperature rapidly to 500 °C or 825 °C. It’s ideal for sterilizing glassware, metal tools, and heat-resistant materials in laboratories, medical facilities, and industrial settings.
The unit offers two fixed sterilization temperatures—500 °C and 825 °C—that can be selected via its front-panel switch for different levels of microbial inactivation and material treatment.
3. How quickly does it reach sterilization temperature?
The SAS-3000 achieves 825 °C in roughly 20 minutes from ambient temperature, allowing fast turnaround for multiple sterilization or annealing cycles.
4. What are its chamber dimensions and capacity?

The internal chamber measures φ14 mm by 140 mm depth, accommodating small flared tubes or similarly sized items. Its overall footprint is 100 × 185 × 180 mm, making it easy to fit on standard workbenches.
5. What electrical requirements does it have?

Two variants exist: the Japanese model runs on 100 VAC 50/60 Hz with a 3-pin plug, while the international version is wired for 220 VAC 50/60 Hz using the same plug style. No special transformer is needed beyond the correct outlet and wiring.
6. How do I switch between the 500 °C and 825 °C modes?
A simple selector on the control panel toggles between the two temperature presets. The device will then automatically ramp up to the chosen setpoint.

The SAS-3000 incorporates thermal fuses and an over-temperature cut-off sensor to prevent runaway heating. An interlock mechanism stops the heater if the chamber door is opened at temperatures above 100 °C, and an audible alarm indicates the end of each cycle.
8. How should I maintain and clean the unit?

Leave the sterilizer to cool completely before cleaning. Wipe the exterior with a damp cloth and mild detergent. Inspect the power cord and plug for damage periodically. No internal user-serviceable parts are exposed—any sensor calibration or major repairs should be performed by authorized technicians.
The SAS-3000 meets CE and RoHS directives for electrical safety and environmental compliance. Regional certificates such as CSA or UL may apply depending on the distributor.

Common accessories include stainless-steel sample holders, ceramic stands to insulate items from direct chamber walls, and custom flared tube racks. Some distributors also offer a data-logging module for temperature monitoring.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ): KAISE KT-2011 Digital Multimeter:
1/ What is the KAISE KT-2011 digital multimeter and who is it designed for?

The KT-2011 is a handheld, high-performance digital multimeter offering up to 500,000 counts. It’s engineered for electronics technicians, field service engineers, and laboratory users who need precise measurements and data-logging capabilities.
2/ What measurement functions and ranges does the KT-2011 support?
The KT-2011 covers all standard multimeter functions.

column3: DC voltage: 500 mV, 5 V, 50 V, 500 V, 1000 V
AC voltage: 500 mV, 5 V, 50 V, 500 V, 1000 V
DC current: 500 µA, 5000 µA, 50 mA, 500 mA, 5 A, 10 A
AC current: 500 µA, 5000 µA, 50 mA, 500 mA, 5 A, 10 A
Resistance: 500 Ω, 5 kΩ, 50 kΩ, 500 kΩ, 5 MΩ, 50 MΩ
Continuity test with buzzer
Diode test
Frequency measurement up to 999,999 Hz

column2: 3/ How accurate is the KT-2011 when measuring DC voltage?
The DC voltage accuracy is 0.03% of reading, making it suitable for demanding calibration tasks and precision electronics work.
4/ How is the KT-2011 powered and what is its expected battery life?
It uses a single 9 V battery (6F22/006P). Under typical lab or field use, you can expect 100–150 hours of continuous operation before the low-battery indicator appears.
5/ How do I turn the meter on/off and select a measurement mode?

column3: Turn the rotary selector to your desired function (e.g., DCV, Ω, DCA).
To power off, rotate the selector fully to “OFF.”
Always start in a higher range if you’re unsure of the signal magnitude.

column2: 6/ How should I connect the test leads?

column3: Insert the black lead into the COM socket.
For voltage, resistance, frequency, and diode: insert the red lead into the V/Ω/Hz socket.
For current measurements up to 500 mA: use the mA socket; for up to 10 A: use the 10 A socket.

column2: 7/ How do I measure DC voltage?

column3: Set the selector to DCV.
Connect black probe to the negative terminal, red probe to the positive terminal.
Read the value on the display.
If “OL” appears, switch to a higher range.

column2: 8/ How do I measure AC voltage?

column3: Set the selector to ACV.
Connect probes as you would for DC.
Observe the waveform stability on the bar graph for best accuracy.

column2: 9/ How do I measure DC and AC current?

column3: Choose the correct current socket (mA or 10 A).
Set the selector to DCA (DC current) or ACA (AC current).
Break the circuit and connect the meter in series.
Reverse polarity if the reading shows negative when measuring DC.

column2: 10/ How do I measure resistance and test continuity?

column3: Set the selector to Ω.
Place probes across the component or circuit.
A reading near zero indicates continuity; a buzzer will sound if resistance is very low.

column2: 11/ How do I use the Max/Min recording function?

column3: Press the Max/Min button once to enter recording mode.
The display toggles through maximum, minimum, ΔMax-Min, and live readings.
Press again to exit back to normal measurement.

column2: 12/ What is the bar-graph indicator and how is it useful?

column3: The 60-segment bar graph updates at 60 Hz.
It visually tracks rapid signal changes that numbers alone might miss.

column2: 13/ How do I change the sampling rate?

column3: Press the SAMPLE button to toggle between 50,000 samples per second and 500,000 samples per second.
Use the lower rate to conserve battery life when you don’t need ultra-fast capture.

column2: 14/ How do I replace the battery and how is low battery indicated?

column3: When the battery icon appears on the LCD, open the rear battery cover.
Replace the old 9 V battery with a fresh one, observing polarity.
Tighten the cover to maintain safety ratings.

column2: 15/ How do I check and replace the protective fuses?

column3: Remove the back cover to access the fuse compartment.
The mA range fuse is typically 250 mA/600 V; the 10 A range fuse is 11 A/1000 V.
Replace with manufacturer-specified fuses only.

column2: 16/ What error messages might appear and how do I troubleshoot?

column3: “OL”: Overload – switch to a higher range or check connections.
“Err”: Internal error – power cycle the meter; if it persists, seek authorized repair.
Blank or flickering display: Check the battery and fuse condition.

column2: 17/ What safety precautions should I follow?

column3: Never exceed rated input limits.
Do not touch metal probe tips when measuring live circuits.
Disconnect test leads before changing settings.
Store in a dry environment and avoid mechanical shocks.

column2: 18/ What accessories come with the KT-2011?

column3: Standard test leads
Spare fuses for mA and 10 A ranges
Holster/carrying case
User manual

column2: 19/ What are the physical dimensions and weight?

column3: Dimensions: 186 mm × 87 mm × 35 mm (H×W×D)
Weight: 390 g (excluding holster)

column2: 20/ Does the KT-2011 support PC connectivity or data logging?

column3: Yes, it features a PC-link function for downloading readings to a computer.
Requires optional interface cable and dedicated software.

column2: 21/ What warranty and technical support are available?

column3: Typically covered by a 12-month manufacturer’s warranty.
Please contact QTE Technologies (qtetech.com/en).

column2: Deep Groove Metric Ball Bearings - Open Type

This range of ball bearings from SKF are open ended, deep groove metric ball bearings, making them extremely versatile for a wide range of applications. SKF single row deep groove ball bearings are available in bore diameters from 3mm to 95mm, so there is sure to be a ball bearing to suit your application.

Why choose open-ended ball bearings? Open bearings have an open side, meaning the balls are visible. This means there are no seals or shields. Open bearings are best suited for environments where the bearings do not come into contact with dirt, as this can damage the bearing. Instead, open ball bearings allow the internal lubricant to move freely around the bearing, allowing for smooth operation. Why choose single-row deep groove ball bearings? This type of ball bearing is the most common because of its versatility. It is ideal for high speeds, excels at handling radial loads, and requires very little maintenance. ""Deep groove"" refers to the race (the groove in which the balls sit). Therefore, the spacing between the inner and outer rings is wider than the diameter of the balls. This allows room for the rubber seal. Why choose steel ball bearings? Steel is the best material for ball bearings because it gives you strength and reliability while remaining corrosion resistant. Steel ball bearings are a good choice for installations because they require very little maintenance and are designed for a long life.

column1: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ):
1/ Can the LZ-990 measure on curved surfaces?
Yes, stable readings are possible on convex or concave surfaces with radii ≥ 10mm, provided the probe maintains full contact.
2/ How do I switch between µm and mil units?
Navigate to Unit Setting in the main menu and select either µm or mils. The change takes effect immediately.
3/ What causes large measurement deviations?
Deviations often stem from uncalibrated zero reference, dirty probe tip, or weak battery. Re-zero, clean the probe, and replace batteries as needed.
4/ How many calibration curves can I store?
The LZ-990 holds 16 calibration curves total: 8 for electromagnetic induction and 8 for eddy-current.
5/ Is manual substrate selection required?
No. The gauge auto-detects the substrate and switches measurement methods automatically.
6/ How do I print results on site?
Attach the optional VZ-380 printer via RS-232C; select Print from the data output menu to generate instant hardcopies.
7/ What standard coatings can it measure?
Paints, plating, anodic oxide, lacquers, resins, plastics, and other non-magnetic/insulating coatings on metallic substrates.
8/ What software is available for data logging?
The LDL-01 Data Logger Software enables CSV exports and trend analysis when connected via USB.
9/ Operation Guidelines
- Ensure the test surface is clean, dry, and free of oil or debris.
- Hold the probe perpendicular and apply gentle, consistent pressure.
- Read the thickness value on the backlit LCD; choose µm or mils via the Unit Setting menu.
- For uneven coatings, take multiple measurements and calculate the average for accurate assessment.
- Rely on the gauge’s auto-zero feature periodically to maintain precision.
10/ Maintenance & Care
- Wipe the probe tip and housing with a soft, dry cloth after use.
- Replace AAA batteries promptly when low-battery indication appears to prevent measurement drift.
- Store the gauge and accessories in the protective pouch to avoid impacts or moisture exposure.
- Schedule recalibration every 3 - 6 months or after 5000 measurements, whichever comes first, to comply with quality standards.

Frequently Asked Questions about the Dahle 00561 Paper Cutter:
1/ What is the Dahle 00561 paper cutter?

The Dahle 00561 is a professional‐grade guillotine trimmer designed for offices, print shops, and home studios. It features hardened Solingen steel blades, an automatic clamp, and a non-slip table for precision cuts.
- Maximum cutting capacity: 3.5mm stack height (approx. 35 sheets of 80 gsm paper)
- Cardstock and mat board up to 3.5mm thick
- Thin vinyl, foam board, and plastic sheets
4/ How do the self-sharpening blades work?
The upper blade slides at an angle across the lower counter-blade, honing itself on each stroke. This continuous edge-refinement keeps cuts clean and the blade sharp over extended use.
5/ How long will the blades last and when should they be replaced?

Blade life depends on material and frequency of use. Cutting only office paper can extend life to several thousand cuts, while frequent cardstock or vinyl cuts wear blades faster. Replace blades when cuts begin to tear or fray.
6/ Can the blades be sharpened or do they need replacing?

Both upper and lower Solingen steel blades are resharpenable. However, because replacement blades (part no. 01561) are affordable and easy to install, most users opt for new blades once performance declines.
7/ How do I replace the blade?
- Remove the two screws securing the upper blade holder.
- Lift out the old blade assembly.
- Position the new blade (01561) in the holder.
- Reinstall and tighten the screws evenly.
- Test cut on scrap paper to ensure proper alignment.
- Automatic clamp holds material firmly, preventing slippage and hand proximity to the blade.
- Unique Dahle safety guard covers the blade edge when not cutting.
- Non-slip rubber feet keep the cutter stable during operation.
9/ What is the function of the automatic clamp?
An integrated spring-loaded clamp evenly compresses your stack as you cut, eliminating manual pressure and ensuring consistently straight cuts.
10/ How does the safety guard work?
A transparent guard automatically swings over the blade when the handle is lowered, providing a clear view of the cutting line while shielding fingers from the edge.
11/ How do I use the magnetic backstop to set cutting lengths?
Slide the magnetic backstop along either of the two scale bars until it clicks at your desired measurement. It locks in place to guide repeat cuts at the same length.
12/ What do the printed scale lines and numbers represent?
Grids, millimeter scales, and angle lines correspond to both metric and common paper formats (including European sizes) and standard angles (e.g., 45°) for quick alignment.
13/ How do I ensure accurate 90° cuts?
Align your material flush against the backstop’s 0 mm mark and verify the blade handle is perpendicular to the table before cutting. The dual mm-marked scale bars help maintain perfect right angles.
14/ What happens if I exceed the specified cutting capacity?
Pushing beyond 3.5mm (about 35 sheets of 80 gsm) risks blade damage, torn cuts, and overstressing the clamp. Always respect capacity limits for best results and safety.
15/ How should I maintain and clean the cutter?
- After each session, brush off paper debris from the table, clamp, and blade area.
- Wipe surfaces with a dry cloth; avoid harsh solvents on the scale markings.
- Lubricate the pivot and clamp rails with light machine oil every 3 - 6 months.
16/ What are common issues and their solutions?
- Paper slipping: clean clamp surface and apply silicone lubricant to rails.
- Blade dragging: check screw tension on blade holder, clear debris, or replace blade.
- Faded scales: gently clean with a damp cloth; avoid bleach or strong alcohol.
- Replacement blade set (upper & lower): part no. 01561

The blowgun body is constructed from durable acetal plastic (POM) that insulates against cold media, and the blow tube is made of brass. It operates reliably from –20 °C to +60 °C.

The FI value is a pollution index that determines the degree of pollution of trace amounts of suspended solids and colloidal substances contained in water. In recent years, FI value measurement has become increasingly important because it is much more sensitive than the turbidity measurement method using scattered light. This measurement method involves filtering the test water using a 0.45μm, 47mm diameter membrane filter under a constant pressure of 0.20MPa.
①Measure the time (t0) required to filter the first 500 mL.
②After 15 minutes of continuous filtration, measure the time (t₀) required to filter 500 mL in the same manner. Calculate the FI value using the following formula.

Frequently Asked Questions for the T&D TR-72NW-S Wired LAN Temperature & Humidity Data Logger:
1. What is the TR-72NW-S and what is it used for?
The TR-72NW-S is a 2-channel temperature and humidity data logger from T&D Corporation featuring a wired LAN interface for automatic data upload.
It’s designed to monitor environmental conditions in storage areas, laboratories, pharmaceutical warehouses, food facilities, and other critical spaces.
2. What are the measurement ranges and accuracies?
3. What power supply does it require?
The unit draws power from an external AC adapter (AD-05A2 or AD-05C2), accepting 100–240 VAC and outputting 5 VDC.
It does not contain an internal battery, so continuous AC connection is required for logging.
The TR-72NW-S has an Ethernet (RJ-45) port supporting DHCP or static IP.
You configure network settings via the front-panel buttons and LCD, then plug a standard LAN cable into your switch or router for automatic data uploads.
It stores up to 1,000,000 readings (temperature and humidity pairs).
When the memory is full, it overwrites the oldest data in a first-in, first-out manner.
6. Can I adjust the logging interval?
Yes. You can set the recording interval anywhere between 10 seconds and 24 hours to suit detailed or long-term monitoring needs.
7. How do I retrieve the recorded data?
Automatic: Data is pushed to the free T&D WebStorage Service or to your local PC running T&D Data Server.
Manual: Connect via USB Mini-B to a computer with the “TR7 for Windows” software to download CSV files and generate reports.
8. Which software and apps are available?
TR7 for Windows: configure settings, download data, export graphs.
T&D Graph: visualize data and print reports on PC.
T&D Thermo (iOS/Android): view real-time graphs and alerts on smartphones.
T&D Data Server: local server software for data reception and storage.
When temperature or humidity exceeds set limits, the TR-72NW-S will:
Send email or SMS alerts via WebStorage Service or Data Server.
Display a warning icon on the LCD.
Log the alarm event with a timestamp.
10. How do I set alarm thresholds?
Use the ▲/▼ buttons and the Set key to enter the “Alarm Set” menu.
Select the channel, input high/low threshold values, then save and exit.
11. What maintenance and calibration are recommended?
Clean the sensor with compressed air or a soft cloth every six months.
Have the temperature and humidity sensors calibrated by a certified lab every 1–2 years.
12. How can I upgrade the firmware?
Connect the logger to a PC via USB, launch TR7 for Windows, and load the firmware file provided by T&D.
13. What are the installation and mounting options?
You can mount it on a wall using the TR-07K2 bracket or place it on a flat surface.
For wall mounting, drill two holes 60 mm apart, hang the bracket, then secure the logger in place.
14. Can I replace or extend the external humidity sensor?
Yes. Compatible extension cables include TR-1C30 (3 m) and TR-5C10 (10 m).
Ensure you use T&D sensors such as THA-3001 or THA-3151 for full compatibility.
15. What common issues might I encounter and how do I troubleshoot?
No LAN connection: check DHCP/static IP settings, network cable, and link LED.
Data not uploading: verify WebStorage Service account or Data Server status, then review the error log.
LCD unreadable: perform a factory reset by pressing the Reset button.

The machine handles twist drill bits with diameters from 10mm up to 20mm.

- Mount the point-setting gauge into the chuck.

- After each 15-minute use, power off and allow a 5 - 10 minute cool-down.

- Inspect the grinding wheel regularly; replace if deep grooves or balance issues appear.
13/ When should I replace the grinding wheel?
Replace the wheel when you notice any of the following:
- Deep abrasive grooves that affect bit geometry
- Cracks, chips, or signs of imbalance

- Always wear eye protection and hearing protection.

- Machine won’t start: check power supply, fuse, and plug connection.

111-67209,HAKKO FR810B-81 Hot air type parts remover (700W, 100V, 2-pole grounded plug)","

column2: High-output 670W heater and large air volume for improved work efficiency
Added vacuum pickup function for easy and safe removal
Preset link function allows creation of simple profiles
Further evolution of high-output, high-airflow SMD rework station
High output and large air volume to meet the needs of ""quick removal""

By increasing the volume and power of hot air, the same work effect can be achieved in approximately one-third of the time compared to conventional methods, and the thermal impact on circuit boards and components can be reduced.
* Both the temperature and airflow were set to maximum, and the time it takes for a connector soldered onto a ceramic board to heat up to 200°C was verified.
The FR-810B maintains the high output and large air volume that were the hallmarks of the conventional FR-810, while adding two new features: a vacuum pickup and a pickup indicator.

The risks involved in SMD rework include damaging the board with tweezers when removing the component from the board, or lifting the component and peeling off the land when the solder is not yet fully melted. The two new functions of the FR-810B make it possible to remove components without damaging the land on the board.
Improved temperature characteristics with the adoption of a new nozzle
By providing a hole in the top of the nozzle, hot air convection occurs inside the nozzle, allowing the outside and center of the nozzle to be heated evenly, improving workability (BGA nozzle only).

The vacuum pickup allows the component to be picked up by suction. Once the component is picked up, the spring mechanism lifts it up when the solder melts. This prevents mistakes such as forcibly pulling up the component and peeling off the land.
Pickup timing is clear at a glance! Pickup indicator

By setting the vacuum pick-up function in advance, when the solder melts and the component is automatically picked up, an indicator will rise up, allowing you to see the moment the component is picked up.

Even if the component is hidden by the nozzle and it is not possible to see the moment the solder melts, it is possible to easily and safely pick up the component because it is clear that removal has been completed.
Nozzles can be quickly replaced to suit a wide variety of parts.
The heater can be easily and reliably replaced.
Conventional nozzles can also be used
By aligning the screw fastening part with the convex part and attaching it, you can use a conventional nozzle.
Timer function for constant working time
This prevents parts from overheating and makes repetitive work easy.
Preset link function allows simple profile creation

By connecting the timer function and the registered preset mode, you can create a simple temperature profile (up to 5 steps can be created). The working time is constant, preventing overheating of parts and making it easier to repeat work, and it also supports advanced removal work. Workability is greatly improved.

Designed with safety and energy saving in mind. When the iron is placed in the iron holder, the auto sleep function is activated, the cool down starts, and the tool automatically goes into standby mode. In addition, if no operation is performed for 30 minutes, the auto shutoff function is activated and the tool also goes into standby mode. Access to various settings can be restricted by password setting, making management easy.
Low-cost rework system can be constructed as an option
By using the grip fixture, board holder, and bottom heater, a low-cost rework system can be constructed, enabling further standardization of work.
Lead-free recommended: This product is also recommended for work using lead-free solder.
RoHS compliant (as of July 2024): This product complies with the regulatory values ​​of the 10 substances prohibited by the European RoHS Directive.

FAQ – CHIYODA SEIKI SRA-A Acetylene Pressure Regulator (0.1–0.13 MPa):
1/ What gas is the SRA-A regulator designed for? The SRA-A model is specifically engineered for acetylene use and should not be used with any other gases to ensure safety and performance.
2/ What outlet pressure range can be set? The outlet (secondary) pressure is adjustable between 0.01 MPa and 0.13 MPa, ideal for low-pressure welding and cutting applications.
3/ What’s the maximum allowable inlet pressure? The inlet (primary) pressure must not exceed 2.5 MPa; operating above this limit may damage the regulator and compromise safety.
4/ What flow rate does the regulator support? At an inlet pressure of 0.05 MPa, the SRA-A can deliver approximately 2 m³/h of acetylene gas.

5/ How do I connect the regulator to my system? The inlet port features a male thread M16 × P1.5 on the left side. The outlet connects to a low-pressure supply hose. Always ensure a tight seal to prevent leaks.
6/ Does it include a pressure gauge and flame arrester? Yes. The SRA-A comes integrated with a pressure gauge and a flame arrester to prevent flashback into the regulator and cylinder.

7/ How does the SRA-A maintain stable outlet pressure? A free-slide piston is compressed by an adjustable spring. Turning the adjustment screw changes spring tension, modulating flow area and holding outlet pressure constant despite flow variations.

8/ How do I adjust the outlet pressure? Rotate the adjustment knob to increase or decrease spring force. Monitor the pressure gauge until you reach the desired outlet pressure, then lock the knob in place.
9/ What installation precautions should I follow?
- Clean the piping of debris that might jam the piston.
- Apply thread sealant compatible with acetylene.
- Mount the regulator upright, following manufacturer orientation guidelines.

10/ What maintenance schedule is recommended? Inspect and recalibrate the pressure gauge, verify piston and spring condition every 6 months or after 1000 operating hours. Replace any worn components promptly.

1/ How the ST-6 series works (principles and variants)

- The ST series is a needle-and-nozzle type precision spray valve where the needle retracts to open the liquid path and the atomizing air shapes the spray pattern; the ST family offers multiple body styles, nozzle sizes, and liquid adjusters to suit varied applications.

- Two main control axes determine output: mechanical needle stroke (or actuator position) and atomizing/air pressure; liquid flow is a function of nozzle orifice, pressure differential, and liquid viscosity.
2/ Performance factors and how to interpret the 0 - 390 mL/min rating

- The published flow range 0 - 390 mL/min is a maximum theoretical range under manufacturer-referenced conditions; actual flow depends on liquid viscosity, supply pressure, needle opening, and any inline flow restrictions.

- For low-viscosity solvents near water-like viscosity, approaching the upper flow limit requires higher supply pressure and full needle opening; for high-viscosity fluids the achievable flow at the same pressure will be significantly lower.
- Use empirical bench tests (measured dispensed volume over time at set pressure and stroke) to map operating points for each fluid and setup; save those operating points for repeatability.

- Thread connection: install with correct G1/8 sealing method (PTFE tape or compatible gasket) and torque to prevent leaks without deforming the valve body; avoid over-torquing which can stress the plated brass body.

- Air and liquid supplies: install dedicated filters and pressure regulators upstream. Use a 5 - 20 µm liquid filter and a coalescing/regulating air filter for atomizing air. Place an isolation valve and a purge/flush port on the liquid line for maintenance.

- Mounting: secure valve to a rigid bracket to avoid vibration; when using long nozzles or extensions verify alignment so the valve’s spray axis is perpendicular to the target. The ST series supports long-nozzle attachments for special geometries.
- Clean system and install a clean nozzle and needle.
- Set liquid supply pressure low and atomizing air to manufacturer-recommended start pressure (if available), then gradually increase.
- Open needle stroke incrementally until a stable spray pattern forms; for fine atomization favor higher atomizing air at smaller needle openings.
- Measure flow at each setting: dispense into a graduated container for a timed period and calculate mL/min. Record pressure, stroke, and measured flow for repeatability.
- Adjust atomizing air vs liquid stroke for the desired droplet size and pattern width; if pattern widens but droplets are coarse, increase atomizing air or reduce stroke.

- Clean immediately after color or material changes and at regular intervals: flush with a compatible solvent, then disassemble nozzle and needle for visual inspection and ultrasonic cleaning if required. Avoid hard metal brushes that deform the orifice.

- Inspect nozzle orifice and needle for wear, burrs, or deformation; replace nozzle/needle when orifice diameter changes or pattern degrades. Keep spare nozzles, needles, O-rings, and springs on hand to minimize downtime.
- Replace seals and O-rings when chemical compatibility is in doubt or when leaks occur; store valves with needle retracted and solvent-filled when idle long-term to prevent drying and caking.
- Clogged nozzle or decreased flow: flush with solvent, remove and inspect nozzle; confirm upstream filter not blocked and supply pressure adequate.
- Irregular spray pattern or tailing: check needle seating for damage; inspect nozzle for partial blockage or eccentric wear; verify stable supply pressures and that atomizing air is clean and dry.
- Excessive overspray or misting: reduce atomizing air or increase needle opening for larger droplets; consider switching nozzle size if coverage needs change.
- Leaks at thread connection: replace sealing tape/gasket and re-torque to spec; replace worn O-rings.
- Flow lower than catalog spec: verify test conditions (pressure and viscosity) were equivalent to manufacturer’s; higher-viscosity fluids and pressure losses in tubing reduce flow.

- Validate flow with timed gravimetric or volumetric collection for each fluid type and temperature. Record: liquid pressure, atomizing air pressure, needle stroke (or actuator displacement), nozzle ID, fluid viscosity and temperature.

- Measure particle size distribution using an appropriate spray analyzer if required for process control; catalog average particle size (e.g., ~43 µm) is a guideline, actual PSD varies with settings and fluid.

- Material compatibility: standard nozzle/needle stainless steel (SUS303) and chrome-plated brass body suit many paints, oils, and solvents; for highly corrosive chemistries consult supplier for alternative materials or coatings.
- Safety: handle flammable solvents in ventilated areas, use grounding and bonding for static-sensitive coatings, and follow local regulations for solvent handling and waste disposal.
- Filters: 5 - 20 µm liquid filters recommended; consider in-line pressure gauges and flow meters for closed-loop monitoring.
- Actuation: integrate pneumatic or electric actuators for repeatable cycle control; control schemes can enable pulsed sprays, multi-shot dosing, or continuous operation per production need.
- Nozzle variants: the ST family supports multiple nozzle IDs and long-nozzle attachments to tune pattern width and reach.
- Keep a written changeover log with the exact operating pressures and stroke settings for each material and color.
- Implement a quick-change spare head module to reduce downtime during maintenance.
- Schedule preventive replacement intervals for nozzles and needles based on throughput rather than visual condition.

Frequently Asked Questions for the Yokogawa Electric SC92-21-J Portable Conductivity Meter:
1. What is the SC92-21-J and what are its typical applications?

The SC92-21-J is a handheld portable conductivity meter designed by Yokogawa for measuring the conductivity of liquids in the field or laboratory. It provides reliable measurements from low-conductivity water to high-salinity solutions, making it suitable for water quality monitoring, environmental testing, and industrial process control.
2. What measurement ranges and units does it support?

The SC92-21-J covers a broad conductivity range of 0 to 2.00 S/cm and low-conductivity measurements down to 0 to 2.00 µS/cm. It also offers resistivity readings up to 200 MΩ·cm. Users can switch display units between µS/cm, mS/cm, S/cm, and Ω·cm directly on the device.
3. How accurate is the SC92-21-J and what resolution does it offer?

Typical accuracy for the SC92 series is ±1% of the reading, depending on the selected measurement range. Resolution can be as fine as 0.01 µS/cm in the lowest range and 0.001 mS/cm in higher ranges, ensuring precise readings across various sample types.
4. What safety precautions should I follow when using the SC92-21-J?

Do not use the device in environments with the risk of electrical shock and avoid touching the electrode immediately after immersion in very hot solutions to prevent burns. Handle the glass sensor carefully to avoid breakage and observe electrostatic discharge precautions when inserting batteries or connecting sensors.
5. How do I set up and operate the meter for basic measurements?
Install two AA batteries and power on the device.
Rinse the sensor with distilled water and immerse it fully into the sample.
Gently stir or tap the sensor to release any trapped air bubbles.
Wait for the stability indicator to appear on the screen, then record the measurement.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) for the AS ONE 1-5170-81 HI-1000G Multi-Purpose Laboratory Hot Plate (300 °C, 230 VAC, PID):
1. What is the AS ONE HI-1000G hot plate?

The HI-1000G is a universal laboratory hot plate designed for precise heating up to 300 °C. It combines a large aluminum heating surface with a PID control system and built-in timer functions, making it ideal for chemical, biological, materials-science, and semiconductor prep work.
3. How does PID control work and why is it beneficial?

PID (Proportional–Integral–Derivative) control continuously monitors the difference between setpoint and actual temperature, automatically adjusting heater power to minimize overshoot and oscillation. This delivers fast stabilization and highly repeatable temperature profiles, crucial for sensitive experiments.
4. What timer modes does it support?
The HI-1000G offers three timer functions for automated workflows:
ON timer: delay auto-start of heating
OFF timer: auto-shutoff after a set duration
SV-OFF timer: heat until setpoint is reached, then countdown and shut off These modes help streamline sample prep and free you from manual monitoring.
Manual-reset over-temperature cutout for heater protection
Built-in thermal fuse to prevent runaway heating
Ground-fault protection requiring a properly grounded AC outlet These layers safeguard both samples and users during high-temperature operation.
6. How do I set up and operate the hot plate?
Ensure the main power switch is OFF and plug the unit into a 230 VAC outlet with protective earth.
Turn on the power switch; the display illuminates.
Use the keypad or dial to set desired temperature (0–300 °C) and select a timer mode if needed.
Allow the plate to heat - PID control will stabilize at setpoint.
After use, switch OFF the unit and unplug before cleaning or storage.
7. What are the power requirements and consumption?

The heater draws approximately 900 W at full output and operates from a single-phase 230 VAC ± 15 % supply at 50/60 Hz. Stable input voltage and proper grounding are mandatory to avoid damage or safety hazards.
8. What maximum load can the heating plate support?
The robust aluminum surface carries up to about 10 kg of sample vessel weight without degrading temperature uniformity or structural integrity.
9. How uniform is the temperature across the plate?
At a setpoint of 300 °C, the plate’s temperature variation remains within 4 °C from center to edge, ensuring consistent heating of multiple or larger samples simultaneously.
10. What routine maintenance does the HI-1000G require?
Wipe the cooled plate surface with a soft, damp cloth - avoid harsh solvents.
Inspect and replace the manual-reset thermal fuse and power cord annually.
Verify temperature accuracy yearly with a calibrated thermometer and recalibrate if drift exceeds ± 4 °C.
11. What environment is recommended for safe operation?
Use in a ventilated lab at 5–40 °C ambient temperature and ≤80 % relative humidity (non-condensing). Keep at least 10 cm clearance around the unit to ensure proper heat dissipation.

Frequently Asked Questions for the AS ONE MD-AW2 Water Activity Meter (4-2453-02):
1. What is the MD-AW2 and what does it measure?

The MD-AW2 is a handheld water activity meter designed for quick on-site determination of a sample’s Aw (water activity). It calculates the ratio of the vapor pressure of water in your test sample to that of pure water at the same temperature, delivering a numerical Aw value from 0 to 1.00.

Water activity (Aw) is the ratio of the partial vapor pressure of water in a material to the vapor pressure of pure water under identical conditions. It indicates how much “free” water is available for microbial growth, chemical reactions, and physical changes in foods, pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, and many other products.
3. How does the MD-AW2 measure Aw?

The device uses a capacitance-type humidity sensor inside a sealed sample chamber. Once the sample cup is in place and the chamber closed, the sensor measures the equilibrium humidity and converts it to an Aw reading via embedded algorithms.
4. What are its range, resolution, and accuracy?
Accuracy: ±0.03 Aw from 0 to 0.9 Aw; ±0.04 Aw outside the 0–0.9 Aw range
These specifications ensure reliable control of moisture-sensitive processes and shelf-life predictions.
5. How long does each measurement take?
A typical measurement cycle takes about five minutes from the moment you press the “Measure” button until the Aw value stabilizes on the LCD display.
6. How many results can the MD-AW2 store?
It holds up to 20 readings in its internal memory, enabling quick recall and comparison of recent samples without manual note-taking.
7. What accessories come with the MD-AW2?
3 chemical filters to protect the sensor
1 m USB cable (note: data export via USB is only supported on the MD-AW3 model)
These accessories let you begin measurements immediately and guard sensor longevity.
8. What are sensor filters for, and how often should I replace them?
Filters sit between your sample and the sensor to block volatile chemicals that can degrade the sensor’s performance.
If you perform ≤ 10 measurements per week, replace filters every 6–12 months.
For > 10 measurements per week, replace every 3–6 months.
For continuous (24/7) use, change filters every 2 months.
Neglecting filter changes may lead to sensor failure, which is not covered by warranty.

This “tune-up” prevents wear-related issues, maintains measurement accuracy, and extends your instrument’s lifespan.
10. How do I operate the MD-AW2?
Install two AA batteries in the compartment.
Place a filled sample cup on the holder inside the chamber.
Wait ~5 minutes for the Aw reading to stabilize on the LCD.
Save the result or manually record it, then remove the cup and clean for reuse.
11. Are there samples the MD-AW2 should not measure?
Do not use it for high-sugar syrups, alcoholic or highly acidic samples (e.g., vinegar), as these can damage the sensor and yield invalid readings.

Q1. How does ultrasonic cleaning work?

Ultrasonic waves at 40 kHz generate microscopic cavitation bubbles in the liquid. When these bubbles collapse, they produce high-velocity micro-jets that dislodge contaminants from surfaces, even in blind holes and crevices.
Q2. How should I prepare the cleaner before use?
Fill the tank with water or a recommended ultrasonic detergent, ensuring the fluid covers your items but stays below the MAX level.
To degas, run the unit empty for 3–5 minutes; this removes dissolved gases for more effective cavitation. Then drain and refill before cleaning your samples.
Q3. What is the recommended cleaning time?
Stubborn deposits: up to 30 minutes or multiple shorter cycles.
Set the time using the ▲/▼ buttons on the control panel; the display counts down once ultrasound starts.
Q4. Do I need to use the heater?
Heating (20–60 °C) speeds removal of oils, greases, and organics.
For heat-sensitive samples (plastics, electronics), operate at room temperature to prevent damage.
Stainless steel basket: prevents direct contact with the bottom, protecting the transducer.
Lid: reduces evaporation, minimizes noise, and maintains temperature.
Drain valve: allows easy fluid removal without tilting the unit.
Q6. Can I use organic solvents directly in the tank?

No. Do not pour flammable solvents (e.g., acetone, alcohol) into the tank. If solvent cleaning is required, place the solvent in a sealed container and immerse it in the water bath, never add it directly to the tank.
Q7. How do I maintain and clean the unit?
After each use: power off, drain the solution, rinse with clean water, and dry thoroughly.
Replace cleaning solution every 3–5 uses or when it becomes discolored.
Inspect O-rings, gaskets, and the drain valve for wear; replace if leaking.
Q8. What if the cleaner does not operate?
No ultrasound: check the power cord, fuse, and main switch.
No heating: verify the heating element and thermostat.
Excessive vibration or noise: ensure samples aren’t touching the tank walls or bottom.
Never run the cleaner without liquid (dry run damages the transducer).
Keep hands and loose objects away from the liquid surface during operation.
Follow lab safety guidelines when handling detergents and hot fluids.

111-68622,Sunon MB45101V2-000U-A99 Axial Fan (12VDC, 45ｘ45ｘ10mm)","

column2: Sunon DRmAgLev Axial Fan, 45x45mm - MB Series

An axial fan is a device that uses a motor to rotate blades housed in a square or circular frame to create airflow. The rotating fan blades draw air into the fan, force it over a surface, and expel it in the same direction for cooling. Axial fans are a critical component in ensuring the smooth operation of machinery and electronic equipment. Cooling equipment is important because overheating can have serious consequences, including premature component degradation, shortened lifespan, and sometimes complete failure.
Sunon DRmAgLev Axial Fan, 45x45mm - MB Series

Sunon's DR (Dust-Resistant) mAgLev DC axial fan products offer cost-effective solutions for all your cooling requirements. DRmAglev fans are developed using magnetic levitation technology to provide high performance, low noise, and long life. The Vapo bearing system and shaft never come into contact during operation, resulting in zero friction no matter how the fan is mounted. Additionally, DRmAglev fans use innovative Seal and Clip (S;C) and Blank and Seamless (B;S) technologies, enhancing dust resistance and oil leakage prevention. DRmAglev axial fans also incorporate an auto-restart function.
What is Blank and Seamless Technology?
Blank and Seamless Technology (B;S) protects the fan by preventing oil leakage. Retaining lubrication is essential to keeping the Vapo bearings working properly.
What is Seal and Clip Technology?
Seal and Clip Technology (S;C) is a technology developed to enhance motor performance and prevent dust intrusion, thereby extending motor life.

If the motor is locked and power continues to be supplied, the coil temperature may rise. The auto-restart feature temporarily cuts power to the motor to prevent unnecessary temperature rise. Once the locked fan rotor is freed, the fan will restart.
Features and Benefits: Rugged thermoplastic PBT UL94V-0 frame and blade, ideal for harsh environments

Compact size allows for integration into space-limited equipment. Compact package with fan motor and central impeller hub integrated. Aerodynamically designed blades for high efficiency and low noise. Seal and Clip (S;C) design for excellent dust resistance. Innovative Blank and Seamless (B;S) technology for no oil leakage. Sophisticated design for maximum efficiency and performance. Available in low, medium, high and extra high speeds.
Compatible with 5 V dc, 12 V dc, and 24 V dc supply voltages. Low vibration, frictionless, and long life of 60,000 hours at 40°C.
There are 4 x 4.3mm holes in the four corners of the outer frame of the fan.
The electrical connection is made using two 26 AWG wires, 300mm long (red +) (black -).
Finger guards are available separately. See part number 544-0964. Finger guards are designed to prevent contact with rotating parts.

This is a black globe type heatstroke index meter that conforms to JIS B 7922 Class 2.
It incorporates a high-performance Swiss-made sensor that measures three elements: black globe temperature, temperature, and humidity, and calculates the Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) index.
The bright LCD panel, large screen, and large numbers make the WBGT value easy to read, and when the heatstroke warning level is reached, an alarm will sound with one of four warning levels.

(*Alarm can be switched on/off, however, if the danger level is reached, a warning alarm will sound even if the alarm is off.) When the danger level is reached, a lamp will light up in addition to the alarm, making it useful in the dark.
This universal design, featuring an alarm and indicator light, ensures safe and easy use for individuals with visual or hearing impairments.
Because it is equipped with a black globe to measure solar radiation and radiant heat, it can measure the heat index (WBGT) even in direct sunlight.
It can be used both indoors and outdoors by switching between IN and OUT.
There are four possible installation methods.
1. Stand: The included stand allows you to use it upright on a tabletop.
The stand is circular with a diameter of approximately 6.5 cm, making it less likely to tip over and allowing for stable placement.
2. Magnet: The unit has a built-in magnet on the back, so it can be attached to metal walls, desks, lockers, etc.

(※Wall mounting outdoors is not recommended as ambient temperatures and other factors may be higher than usual, making accurate measurements impossible.) 3. Strap with carabiner: Can be easily attached to your waist or hooks.
By attaching it to your waist, it helps prevent heatstroke while you're working.
4. Tripod: It has a screw hole and can be attached to a tripod.
It can be used off the ground (floor) even in places where there are no hooks or anything similar.

This design takes into account the shape of hot magnetic stirrs, which are often used with oil baths, and features a structure that allows the top plate of the stirrer to be fitted into place.
This prevents the bath from moving or sliding off due to vibrations from agitation.
It fits perfectly with Yamato Scientific's MFD800 and MFH800 magnetic stirrers for synthesis.
Use the recommended oil amount as a guide to reduce wasted oil.
Because the silicone oil used in the bus expands significantly (around 15%) when heated, we have indicated the recommended amount of oil to use on the bus itself.
This helps reduce dangerous oil spills and unnecessary oil usage. (The recommended oil volume differs for 1.0L and 2.2L sizes.)
Safety design with independent overheat protection and heater guards.

It features an independent overheat protection function that automatically shuts off the power in the event of an overheating problem, such as forgetting to add oil or experiencing abnormal heating temperatures due to insufficient oil caused by evaporation.
Additionally, a heater guard is installed to prevent direct contact with the heater unit that heats the oil.
*Do not place objects directly on the heater guard (slatted part).
The reaction solution is precisely heated to the desired temperature.

An optional external temperature sensor is inserted into the sample container (such as a three-neck flask) to measure the temperature of the reaction solution, and the bus is controlled to maintain the desired temperature.
The controller can also display the current temperature of the sample. (Switchable display between the sample temperature and the temperature inside the chamber.)
Oil bath + Mag Mixer MFD800 combination system
We offer oil bath systems that provide the temperature precision and stirring power required for chemical synthesis experiments.
We offer a range of viscosity options, from high to low, in a 3-unit system.
